title: Import and export flows

controls.label: Profiles
controls.visible_when: the Profiles drawer entry is selected
controls.action: Shows the profile list and the import and export menus.

controls.label: Profiles
controls.action: Shows the screen title.

controls.label: Add Profile
controls.action: Opens the submenu with scan, clipboard import, file import, file replace and manual settings.

controls.label: Scan QR code
controls.visible_when: the Add Profile submenu is open
controls.action: Starts ScannerActivity to scan QR codes.

controls.label: Import from Clipboard
controls.visible_when: the Add Profile submenu is open
controls.action: Reads the primary clip, creates one profile per valid ss:// URL, and shows a result snackbar.

controls.label: Import from file…
controls.visible_when: the Add Profile submenu is open
controls.action: Opens a system picker for application/* and text/* documents and appends their profiles.

controls.label: Replace from file…
controls.visible_when: the Add Profile submenu is open
controls.action: Opens the same picker and replaces every profile with the file's profiles.

controls.label: Manual Settings
controls.visible_when: the Add Profile submenu is open
controls.action: Creates a profile seeded with the current feature settings and opens the editor.

controls.label: Export…
controls.action: Opens the export submenu with Export to Clipboard and Export to file….

controls.label: Export to Clipboard
controls.action: Copies every active profile's ss:// URL, joined by newlines, as a sensitive clip.

controls.label: Export to file…
controls.action: Opens a save picker and writes the active profiles as a JSON array.

controls.label: Profile list
controls.action: Shows one row per active profile ordered by userOrder.

controls.label: Profile row
controls.visible_when: one per profile returned by getActiveProfiles()
controls.enabled_when: service state is Stopped, Connecting, or Connected
controls.action: Selects the profile on tap when the service can stop or is stopped; it holds the edit, subscription and share icons.

controls.label: Share
controls.action: Opens a popup menu with QR code and Export to Clipboard.

controls.label: Share popup
controls.action: Shows the QR code and Export to Clipboard items anchored to the share icon.

controls.label: QR code
controls.action: Shows a QR code dialog for this profile's ss:// URL.

controls.label: Export to Clipboard
controls.action: Copies this profile's ss:// URL as a sensitive clip and shows the result snackbar.

controls.label: QR code
controls.visible_when: the QR code item is tapped
controls.action: Shows the encoded profile as an image, or dismisses with an error snackbar.

controls.label: Profile QR code
controls.action: Displays a 264dp black and white QR bitmap.

controls.label: Snackbar
controls.visible_when: an import or export action reports a result
controls.action: Shows Successfully import!, Failed to import., Successfully export!, Failed to export., Please install a file manager like MiXplorer, or an exception message.

controls.label: Url import
controls.visible_when: a VIEW intent with scheme ss opens the app
controls.action: Parses the link and shows the import dialog or the invalid-input toast, then finishes.

controls.label: Add this Shadowsocks Profile?
controls.visible_when: the link yields at least one profile
controls.action: Asks the user to confirm the listed profiles.

controls.label: ss:// URL list
controls.action: Lists one ss:// URL per line.

controls.label: Yes
controls.action: Creates every listed profile and finishes the activity.

controls.label: No
controls.action: Finishes the activity without creating a profile.

controls.label: No valid profile data found.
controls.visible_when: intent.data is null or the link holds no valid profile
controls.action: Shows the Toast and finishes the activity.

controls.label: System file picker (open)
controls.visible_when: Import from file… or Replace from file… is tapped
controls.action: Returns zero or more document URIs of type application/* or text/*.

controls.label: System file picker (save)
controls.action: Asks for a destination and suggests profiles.json with type application/json.

controls.label: Search
controls.action: Filters the profile list by name or host, case-insensitive.

rules.statement: Import from Clipboard creates one profile for each valid ss:// URL in the primary clip.

examples.given: The clipboard holds two valid ss:// URLs.
examples.when: The user taps Import from Clipboard.
examples.then: The list gains two profiles and the snackbar reads Successfully import!.

examples.given: The clipboard holds one valid ss:// URL and one line of plain text.
examples.when: The user taps Import from Clipboard.
examples.then: The list gains one profile and the snackbar reads Successfully import!.

rules.statement: Import from Clipboard shows Failed to import. when no ss:// URL parses or the clipboard cannot be read. It shows the same message when a profile insert throws after some profiles were created.

examples.given: The clipboard holds plain text without ss://.
examples.when: The user taps Import from Clipboard.
examples.then: The snackbar reads Failed to import. and the list does not change.

examples.given: The clipboard is empty.
examples.when: The user taps Import from Clipboard.
examples.then: The null clip throws, the catch block runs, and Failed to import. appears.

examples.given: The clipboard holds two valid ss:// URLs and the second insert throws.
examples.when: The user taps Import from Clipboard.
examples.then: The first profile stays, the second is absent, and the snackbar reads Failed to import.

examples.given: The clipboard holds one valid ss:// URL.
examples.when: The user taps Import from Clipboard.
examples.then: The URL becomes one profile and the snackbar reads Successfully import!.

rules.statement: Each imported profile is inserted with createProfile and appended after the last userOrder.

examples.given: The last stored profile has userOrder 4.
examples.then: The new row is last and its userOrder is 5.

examples.given: Replace mode clears the last stored profile before the first insert.
examples.when: The first imported profile is created.
examples.then: Its userOrder is 0, because the empty table has no maximum order.

rules.statement: An import does not change the selected profile; imported rows stay unselected.

examples.given: Profile A is selected.
examples.then: A stays selected and B is appended without a selected mark.

examples.given: No profile is selected.
examples.then: The new row is appended without a selected mark.

rules.statement: Import from file… opens a picker for application/* and text/* and accepts several documents.

examples.given: Two JSON files hold one profile each.
examples.when: The user selects both files and confirms.
examples.then: Both profiles are imported in one batch.

examples.given: The user has one application/json file and one text/plain file.
examples.when: The user selects both files and confirms.
examples.then: Both documents go to one import batch.

rules.statement: Replace from file… uses the same picker as Import from file… and sets replace mode.

examples.given: The Profiles screen is shown.
examples.when: The user taps Replace from file….
examples.then: The same document picker opens and the result is handled with replace=true.

examples.given: The Profiles screen is shown.
examples.when: The user taps Import from file… and chooses a document.
examples.then: The result is handled with replace=false and no stored profile is deleted.

rules.statement: Replace mode deletes every profile when the first imported profile is created.

examples.given: Two profiles are stored.
examples.when: Replace from file… imports one profile.
examples.then: Only the imported profile remains.

examples.given: Two profiles are stored.
examples.when: Replace from file… reads a file with no valid profile.
examples.then: No profile is deleted, because the clear runs only inside the first create.

rules.statement: Replace mode copies tx and rx from the existing profile with the same formattedAddress.

examples.given: The stored profile for 1.2.3.4:8388 has tx 100 and rx 200.
examples.when: Replace from file… imports 1.2.3.4:8388 with a new password.
examples.then: The imported profile keeps tx 100 and rx 200.

examples.given: The stored profile is 1.2.3.4:8388 with tx 100 and rx 200.
examples.then: The imported profile starts at tx 0 and rx 0, because no formattedAddress matches.

rules.statement: Replace mode takes feature settings from the stored profile whose id equals the selected profile id.

examples.given: The selected profile has id 3 and route bypass-lan.
examples.when: Replace from file… imports a profile without a route field.
examples.then: The imported profile gets route bypass-lan.

examples.given: The selected profile id matches no stored profile.
examples.when: Replace from file… imports a profile without a route field.
examples.then: The imported profile keeps the default route all.

rules.statement: A JSON object is a profile only when server, server_port, password and method are present and non-empty.

examples.given: An object has server, server_port and password but no method.
examples.then: The object is not a profile and its fields are searched instead.

examples.given: An object carries server 198.51.100.7, server_port 8388, a password, and method aes-256-gcm.
examples.then: The object becomes one profile with host 198.51.100.7, remotePort 8388, and the object's password and method.

rules.statement: The JSON importer rejects a server_port that is zero or negative.

examples.given: A file holds an entry with server_port 0 and a valid entry.
examples.then: Only the valid entry becomes a profile.

examples.given: An entry carries server_port 8388 and the other required fields.
examples.then: The entry becomes one profile with remotePort 8388.

rules.statement: A recognized profile object stops the recursive search; the importer does not look inside it.

examples.given: A valid profile object also contains a nested object with a profile.
examples.then: Only the outer profile is returned.

examples.given: An object without a method field holds a nested valid profile.
examples.then: The nested profile is returned.

rules.statement: The JSON importer searches every object field and every array element for profiles.

examples.given: A gui-config.json file holds profiles under configs.
examples.then: Every profile under configs is found.

examples.given: A file holds only a JSON number.
examples.then: The importer finds no profile and the list does not change.

rules.statement: Every imported JSON profile copies the current profile's route, IPv6, metered, per-app proxy settings and DNS over UDP setting.

examples.given: The current profile uses route bypass-china, IPv6 true and DNS over UDP true.
examples.when: A JSON profile without route, ipv6 and udpdns is imported.
examples.then: The imported profile gets bypass-china, IPv6 true and DNS over UDP true.

examples.given: The current profile has proxy apps enabled with bypass true and one package.
examples.when: A JSON profile without proxy_apps is imported.
examples.then: The imported profile gets the enabled flag, bypass and the package list.

examples.given: No profile is selected.
examples.when: A JSON profile without feature fields is imported.
examples.then: The imported profile keeps route all, IPv6 false and DNS over UDP false.

rules.statement: For a profile object that is not a udp_fallback, route, ipv6, metered, proxy_apps and udpdns in the JSON override the inherited values. remote_dns is not inherited, so an absent one keeps the new profile's default dns.google.

examples.given: The current route is all and the JSON field says gfwlist.
examples.then: The imported profile uses gfwlist.

examples.given: The current profile resolves through 1.1.1.1 and the JSON has no remote_dns field.
examples.then: The imported profile keeps dns.google and does not copy 1.1.1.1.

rules.statement: A udp_fallback object is parsed with the fallback flag. Of the feature fields, only plugin, remarks and route are read. The parse then returns before remote_dns, ipv6, metered, proxy_apps and udpdns.

examples.given: A udp_fallback object has a different server and its own ipv6 true.
examples.then: The fallback object's ipv6 is ignored and the fallback keeps the inherited value.

examples.given: A main entry holds a udp_fallback object with its own server, server_port, password, method, plugin obfs-local, plugin_opts obfs=http, remarks UDP fallback, and route bypass-lan.
examples.then: The fallback profile carries plugin obfs-local;obfs=http, remarks UDP fallback, and route bypass-lan, and the main profile's udp_fallback points to it.

rules.statement: A fallback reuses an existing profile with the same host, port, password, method and no plugin. When no profile matches, the fallback is created as a second profile and linked by udpFallback.

examples.given: A stored profile matches the fallback host, port, password and method and has no plugin.
examples.then: The fallback links to that stored profile and no duplicate is created.

examples.given: No stored profile matches the fallback.
examples.then: The fallback is inserted as a second profile and the main profile's udpFallback id names it.

rules.statement: Export to Clipboard joins all active profiles' ss:// URLs with newline characters.

examples.given: Two active profiles exist.
examples.when: The user taps Export to Clipboard.
examples.then: The clip holds the two URLs on separate lines.

examples.given: One active profile exists.
examples.when: The user taps Export to Clipboard.
examples.then: The clip holds that URL and no newline character.

rules.statement: Export to Clipboard marks the clipboard entry as sensitive on Android 7.0 and later.

examples.given: The device runs Android 7.0 or later.
examples.then: The clip description carries EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE true.

examples.given: The device runs Android 6.0.
examples.then: The clip carries no EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE flag.

rules.statement: Export to Clipboard shows Failed to export. when the profile list is null or the clipboard write throws.

examples.given: The clipboard service rejects the write.
examples.when: The user taps Export to Clipboard.
examples.then: The snackbar reads Failed to export.

examples.given: The profile list is non-null and the system clipboard accepts the write.
examples.when: The user taps Export to Clipboard.
examples.then: The clipboard holds the profiles' ss:// URLs joined by newlines and the snackbar reads Successfully export!.

rules.statement: Export to file… writes the active profiles as a pretty-printed JSON array.

examples.given: Two active profiles exist.
examples.when: The user confirms profiles.json in the save picker.
examples.then: The file holds a JSON array indented by two spaces.

examples.given: The active profile list is empty.
examples.when: The user confirms profiles.json in the save picker.
examples.then: The file holds an empty JSON array and no snackbar appears.

rules.statement: The save picker suggests profiles.json and the application/json type.

examples.given: The user taps Export to file….
examples.then: The suggested name is profiles.json and the type is application/json.

examples.given: The export launcher receives an empty input string.
examples.then: The suggested name is still profiles.json and the type is application/json.

rules.statement: Export to file shows no success message. A null serializeToJson result writes nothing. A thrown write shows the exception's readable message.

examples.given: The file is written successfully.
examples.then: No snackbar appears.

examples.given: The output stream throws.
examples.then: The snackbar shows the exception's readable message.

rules.statement: A cancelled export picker writes no file and shows no message.

examples.given: The save picker is open.
examples.then: No file is written and no snackbar appears.

examples.given: The save picker returns a destination document.
examples.then: The document holds the exported profile array as indented JSON and no snackbar appears.

rules.statement: Exported JSON carries plugin, plugin_opts, remarks, route, remote_dns, ipv6, metered, proxy_apps and udpdns.

examples.given: A profile has a plugin, a name and the route bypass-lan.
examples.then: The entry carries plugin, plugin_opts, remarks and route.

examples.given: A profile has proxy apps disabled.
examples.then: proxy_apps carries enabled false and omits bypass and android_list.

rules.statement: plugin and plugin_opts are written only when the plugin id is not empty.

examples.given: A profile has no plugin.
examples.then: The entry has no plugin and no plugin_opts field.

examples.given: A profile has plugin obfs-local;obfs=http.
examples.then: The entry has plugin obfs-local and plugin_opts obfs=http.

rules.statement: udp_fallback is written only when the fallback profile exists and has no plugin.

examples.given: The fallback profile has a plugin.
examples.then: No udp_fallback object is written.

examples.given: The main profile points to a fallback profile whose plugin is empty.
examples.then: The entry holds a udp_fallback object with the fallback's server, server_port, password and method.

rules.statement: The export contains only active profiles; profiles with subscription status Obsolete are excluded.

examples.given: One profile is UserConfigured and one is Obsolete.
examples.then: Only the UserConfigured profile is written.

examples.given: Every stored profile has subscription status Obsolete.
examples.then: The exported JSON array is empty.

rules.statement: Manual Settings creates a profile, copies the current feature settings, and opens the editor.

examples.given: The selected profile uses route bypass-lan.
examples.then: A new profile with route bypass-lan is created and the editor opens for it.

examples.given: No profile is selected.
examples.then: A new profile with the default route all is created and the editor opens.

rules.statement: Manual Settings creates and stores the profile before it opens the editor. The editor's back arrow only finishes the activity and does not delete the row.

examples.given: The user has not saved anything in the editor.
examples.when: The user leaves the editor with the back arrow.
examples.then: The new profile remains in the list.

examples.given: The profile insert throws an SQL exception.
examples.then: The editor does not open and the process crashes.

rules.statement: The row share icon opens a popup with QR code and Export to Clipboard.

examples.given: A profile row is shown.
examples.when: The user taps the share icon.
examples.then: A popup with QR code and Export to Clipboard appears.

examples.given: The service is stopped and a profile row is shown.
examples.when: The user taps the row text instead of the share icon.
examples.then: The profile is selected and no share popup opens.

rules.statement: Export to Clipboard in the row popup copies only that profile's ss:// URL.

examples.given: Three profiles exist.
examples.when: The user exports the second profile from its share popup.
examples.then: The clip holds only the second profile's URL.

examples.given: Three profiles exist.
examples.when: The user taps Export… and then Export to Clipboard in the toolbar.
examples.then: The clip holds all three URLs on separate lines.

rules.statement: The QR dialog encodes the profile's ss:// URL as a 264dp black and white bitmap.

examples.given: A profile is shown.
examples.then: A 264dp square image of black modules on white appears.

examples.given: The URL cannot be encoded.
examples.then: No 264dp image appears and the dialog closes.

rules.statement: The QR encoder passes a UTF-8 hint only when the URL is not ISO-8859-1 encodable. Uri.Builder percent-encodes a non-ASCII name, so only a non-ASCII host can trigger the hint.

examples.given: The profile name contains Chinese characters.
examples.then: The fragment is percent-encoded, the URL stays ASCII, and no CHARACTER_SET hint is passed.

examples.given: The profile host contains characters outside ISO-8859-1.
examples.then: encodedAuthority keeps the non-ASCII text, the URL is not ISO-8859-1 encodable, and CHARACTER_SET UTF-8 is passed.

examples.given: The profile host and name hold ASCII characters only.
examples.then: The URL is ISO-8859-1 encodable, no CHARACTER_SET hint is passed, and the dialog shows the QR bitmap.

rules.statement: A WriterException shows the exception message in a snackbar and dismisses the dialog.

examples.given: The URL cannot be encoded.
examples.then: The snackbar shows the message and the dialog closes.

examples.given: The profile URL encodes without a WriterException.
examples.then: The dialog shows the QR bitmap and no snackbar appears.

rules.statement: A URL without user information is legacy base64 of method:password@host:port, and its plugin and name come from the query and the fragment.

examples.given: The link is ss://base64(method:password@host:port)#name.
examples.then: Method, password, host, port and name are filled in.

examples.given: The link is ss:// followed by base64 text without method:password@host:port.
examples.then: The URL is dropped and no profile is created.

rules.statement: A SIP002 URL decodes base64url user information into method and password.

examples.given: The link is ss://base64url(method:password)@host:port.
examples.then: Method and password come from the decoded user information.

examples.given: The user information decodes to text without a colon.
examples.then: The URL is dropped and no profile is created.

rules.statement: A SIP002 URL takes method and password from the base64url user information. It takes host and port from the text after @ through java.net.URI. Brackets around an IPv6 literal are stripped. Its plugin comes from the query and its name from the fragment.

examples.given: The link is ss://base64url(method:password)@[2001:db8::1]:8388?plugin=obfs-local%3Bobfs%3Dhttp#Work.
examples.then: Host is 2001:db8::1 without brackets, port is 8388, plugin is obfs-local with its options, and the name is Work.

examples.given: The link has an unclosed bracket in the host.
examples.then: The URL is dropped and no profile is created.

rules.statement: An invalid base64 or URI drops that URL and keeps the other parsed URLs.

examples.given: One URL has a malformed base64 body and one URL is valid.
examples.then: Only the valid URL becomes a profile.

examples.given: The text holds two valid ss:// URLs, one in the SIP002 form and one in the legacy form.
examples.then: Both URLs become profiles and neither is dropped.

rules.statement: UrlImportActivity answers only VIEW intents with scheme ss and is excluded from recents.

examples.given: A browser opens an ss:// link.
examples.when: Android resolves VIEW with scheme ss.
examples.then: UrlImportActivity opens as the handler.

examples.given: A browser opens an http:// link.
examples.then: UrlImportActivity is not a handler.

rules.statement: UrlImportActivity parses the link with the current profile as the feature source.

examples.given: A link holds a URL without feature fields.
examples.then: The new profile copies the current profile's feature settings.

examples.given: No profile is selected.
examples.when: The activity parses a URL without feature fields.
examples.then: The new profile keeps the default route all and IPv6 false.

rules.statement: The link dialog title is Add this Shadowsocks Profile? and lists one ss:// URL per line.

examples.given: The link holds two profiles.
examples.then: The title is Add this Shadowsocks Profile? and the message has two lines.

examples.given: The link holds one profile.
examples.then: The title is Add this Shadowsocks Profile? and the message has one line.

rules.statement: Yes creates every listed profile; No or a dismiss finishes without creating any.

examples.given: The dialog lists one profile.
examples.then: The activity closes and the profile count does not change.

examples.given: The dialog lists two profiles.
examples.then: Both profiles are created and the activity finishes.

rules.statement: A link with no valid profile shows the Toast No valid profile data found. and finishes.

examples.given: The link body decodes to no profile.
examples.then: The Toast appears and the activity finishes.

examples.given: The link decodes to one profile.
examples.then: The import dialog shows the profile and the activity stays open until the user answers.

rules.statement: Import and export menu items stay enabled in every service state.

examples.given: The VPN is connected.
examples.when: The user opens the Add Profile or Export submenu.
examples.then: Every import and export item is enabled.

examples.given: The service is Stopped.
examples.when: The user opens the Add Profile submenu and then the Export submenu.
examples.then: Every import and export item is enabled.

rules.statement: When no activity handles the file picker, the snackbar reads Please install a file manager like MiXplorer.

examples.given: No installed app handles the open-document intent.
examples.when: The user taps Import from file….
examples.then: The warning snackbar appears and no picker opens.

examples.given: An installed file manager handles the open-document intent.
examples.when: The user taps Import from file….
examples.then: The document picker opens and no snackbar appears.

rules.statement: The list seeds one default profile when the database is empty, before any import.

examples.given: The profile database is empty.
examples.then: One default profile is created and selected.

examples.given: One profile is stored.
examples.then: No default profile is added and the stored profile stays.

rules.statement: Add Profile, Import from Clipboard, Import from file, Export… and Export to Clipboard declare the letter shortcuts n, v, o, s and c.

examples.given: A hardware keyboard is attached.
examples.when: The user presses the menu shortcut key.
examples.then: The matching menu item runs.

examples.given: The Add Profile submenu is open and a hardware keyboard is attached.
examples.then: Import from file… runs and Replace from file… does not run.

rules.statement: Replace from file…, Manual Settings and Export to file… require Ctrl+Shift with o, n and s.

examples.given: A hardware keyboard is attached.
examples.then: Replace from file… runs.

examples.given: The Add Profile submenu is open and a hardware keyboard is attached.
examples.when: The user presses n without Ctrl+Shift.
examples.then: Manual Settings does not run.

rules.statement: The share icon stays enabled for every row, including the active profile.

examples.given: The VPN runs with profile A selected.
examples.when: The user looks at row A.
examples.then: Its share icon is enabled; only the edit and subscription icons are dimmed.

examples.given: The VPN is stopped and the list holds two profiles.
examples.when: The user taps the share icon on the second row.
examples.then: The share popup opens with QR code and Export to Clipboard.

rules.statement: A profile parsed from an ss:// URL copies the current profile's feature settings.

examples.given: The current profile uses route bypass-lan and udpdns true.
examples.when: A URL without feature fields is imported.
examples.then: The new profile gets route bypass-lan and udpdns true.

examples.given: The current profile uses plugin v2ray-plugin, and the link has no plugin query.
examples.then: The new profile has no plugin, because the copied settings exclude plugin.

rules.statement: The ss:// URL writer puts base64url method:password without padding into encodedAuthority. It brackets an IPv6 host. It adds ?plugin= with percent-encoded plugin options when a plugin is selected. It adds #name when the name is not empty.

examples.given: A profile uses method aes-256-gcm, password p@ss/word, host 2001:db8::1, port 8388, plugin obfs-local with obfs=http, and name Work.
examples.then: The URL is ss://<base64url method:password without padding>@[2001:db8::1]:8388?plugin=obfs-local%3Bobfs%3Dhttp#Work.

examples.given: A profile has no plugin and an empty name.
examples.then: The URL has no ?plugin= query and no #fragment.

rules.statement: The JSON importer builds plugin from plugin and plugin_opts as id;options, and sets the profile name from remarks.

examples.given: A JSON entry has plugin obfs-local, plugin_opts obfs=http and remarks Work.
examples.then: The profile plugin is obfs-local;obfs=http and its name is Work.

examples.given: A JSON entry has no plugin and no remarks fields.
examples.then: The profile plugin is empty and its name is empty.

rules.statement: A JSON error in one document keeps the profiles created before it, continues with the later documents, and rethrows the first error. A read error while advancing to a document stops the later documents. The created profiles stay in both cases.

examples.given: The first document is valid and the second document is malformed JSON.
examples.then: The first document's profiles stay, and the snackbar shows the parse error after the loop.

examples.given: Replace from file… imports a valid first document, then a document whose stream cannot be opened.
examples.then: The stored profiles are already deleted and the first document's profiles stay.

examples.given: Two chosen documents are valid JSON and each holds one profile.
examples.then: Both profiles are created and no snackbar appears.

rules.statement: A replace does not reset the selected profile id. The clear deletes the selected row and the new rows get new ids. No row is selected afterwards, so Core.currentProfile is null.

examples.given: Profile A is selected and a file with one profile is imported in replace mode.
examples.then: The list holds the imported profile, no row is selected, and Core.currentProfile is null.

examples.given: Profile A is selected and the replace file holds a profile with A's address.
examples.then: The imported row keeps A's traffic counters and gets a new id, and no row is selected, so Core.currentProfile is null.

rules.statement: A failure while importing a file is caught and shown in a snackbar with the exception's readable message.

examples.given: A chosen document's JSON is malformed.
examples.then: The snackbar shows the exception message and keeps the profiles already created.

examples.given: A chosen document holds valid JSON.
examples.then: Its profiles are created and no error snackbar appears.

transitions.event: Import from file… or Replace from file… is chosen
the picker returns one or more documents
at least one profile is parsed
no activity handles the picker intent
a document cannot be opened or the import throws
the adapter shows the new rows
the files yield no profile, so the list stays unchanged
the file manager warning snackbar is shown
the exception snackbar is shown and the profiles created before the failure stay
at least one profile is parsed

flows.name: Import profiles from the clipboard

steps.label: start: the user opens the Add Profile menu on the Profiles screen
steps.next: the user taps Import from Clipboard

steps.label: the user taps Import from Clipboard
steps.next: decision: the clip holds at least one ss:// URL — yes

steps.label: decision: the clip holds at least one ss:// URL — yes
steps.next: create one profile per parsed URL

steps.label: decision: no ss:// URL parses or the clipboard cannot be read — no
steps.next: show the Failed to import. snackbar

steps.label: create one profile per parsed URL
steps.next: show the Successfully import! snackbar

steps.label: show the Successfully import! snackbar

notes: All listed files exist and were read. The schema has no menu or toast type. The share popup is recorded as a dialog. The link-import toast is recorded as a snackbar. Scope: U02 owns row tap, edit, delete, reorder and search filtering. U04 records the controls its import and export flows use. The Search item sits in the menu file of this unit, so it is listed here. U02 covers its behavior. The HarmonyOS app implements the import and export model, the menus, the link dialog and the row share menu. The document picker accepts up to 20 files per import. It has no MIME filter, so every document type is selectable. That covers the Android application/* and text/* filter. The save picker offers profiles.json and the .json suffix. It has no MIME type setting. The clipboard export writes newline-joined ss:// URLs. The pasteboard has no sensitive flag. The app marks the data local-only. R-UD-19 and the matching expected steps of TC-U04-12 and TC-U04-18 stay partial. A replace keeps the id and the name of a stored profile with the same address. The counters stay. If that profile was selected, it stays selected. The remarks in the file do not replace the stored name. Android gives the row a new id and copies only the counters. TC-U04-05 records this difference as partial. The JSON import reads proxy_apps and udp_fallback. An imported profile inherits route, ipv6, metered, udpdns and the per-app settings from the selected profile. The editor shows route, IPv6, the Apps VPN mode row and the UDP Fallback row. It has no DNS over UDP control. TC-U04-09 and TC-U04-35 record that display gap as partial. The row share menu opens a QR dialog, so TC-U04-17 matches the Android dialog. The dialog shows a fixed message when the URL is too long. It does not show the exception message from the encoder. TC-U04-19 records that difference as partial. The row clipboard export shows Copy failed when the write throws. TC-U04-29 records that message difference as partial. A file import or a file export shows no message on success. A malformed document shows the parser message and keeps the profiles from the other documents. A read or write failure shows the platform message. Those messages can be English in the Chinese UI. AGENTS.md records this known gap. A link arrives as a dialog on the profile list page. There is no separate import activity or screen. The app handles the ss scheme only. TC-U04-34 records the missing import screen as partial. The app cannot detect that no file manager is installed. TC-U04-20 is android-only. HarmonyOS also has an Import ss:// URL dialog. Android has no such dialog. It is outside this Android specification. The ss:// writer R-UD-52 matches HarmonyOS Profile.toUri. The QR encoder reproduces the output of zxing.
